label: Stop 3: The Cathedral of Our Lady

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Okay. That is a very big tower.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The north tower is 123 meters tall.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It's the tallest in the city.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And it looks a bit lopsided. There's another one next to it.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: There is. The southern tower is shorter, and it has a wooden lantern on top.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: A wooden lantern. On a stone cathedral.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It was meant to be temporary. In 1533, a fire destroyed the wooden roof.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Money meant for a big expansion went to repairs instead.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: In 1536, they put up a wooden lantern as a stopgap.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It's still there.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Nearly 500 years. That's one very successful stopgap.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It's a very Belgian solution. Temporary, and permanent.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: How old is the church?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The story goes back to 1124, when a Romanesque church was founded.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The Gothic church began in 1352, with the choir.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The big north tower was started in 1420 and finished in 1518.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: So almost 100 years on the tower alone.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: And in 1521, Emperor Charles V backed a project called the Nieuw Werck, the New Work, which was meant to make the church about three times larger.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Three times? It's already huge.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: And then the fire came, and the money went elsewhere.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Today the church has six naves and it's 53.6 meters wide.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The part that was never finished is now a garden.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: I love that. A cathedral extension that became a garden.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Now, if you're going in, here is what to look for.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: There are four paintings by Rubens inside.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Four in one church. That's a good start.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Over the high altar, The Assumption of Mary.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: To the left of the altar, The Raising of the Cross.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: To the right, The Descent from the Cross.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: And in a chapel on the right, The Resurrection of Christ.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Do they still hang where they were meant to?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Three of the four hang in their original settings, which is rare.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And the Resurrection?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: That one was commissioned as a memorial for the son-in-law of a printer called Plantin.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: We'll meet his house in a few stops.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Remember the name Moretus.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Moretus. Printer. Got it.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Rubens himself is buried in a different church, Saint James's, not here.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: So don't go looking for his tomb in the cathedral.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Correct.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And practical bits?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Check the opening hours and whether there's a ticket.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Churches can close for services or events.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: And if it's raining, this is your first dry stop of the day.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: These paintings were made for people to pray in front of, so give them a few quiet minutes.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Of course.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Pause here. Go in, if you can.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Take your time.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And outside, afterward?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Step out into the small square by the church front.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: That's the Handschoenmarkt, the Glove Market.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: That's where we'll start the next stop.
